How to Define the First Version of Your Mobile App

Turn an app idea into one complete user journey, a realistic MVP scope and clear acceptance criteria.

By DevMania · 21 September 2026 · 2 min read
Share on LinkedInShare on WhatsApp

In this guide

Choose a repeatable problemDraw the smallest complete journeyLimit the first release deliberatelyDescribe failure statesDecide how to learn

Choose a repeatable problem

A mobile app needs a reason for someone to return. “An app for our business” is too broad. “Let returning customers reorder their usual supplies” is a useful starting point. Identify the user, the trigger and the result they want. Then ask whether a mobile app offers a benefit over the existing website or process.

Draw the smallest complete journey

For a reorder app, the journey could be signing in, selecting a previous order, changing quantities and submitting a request. Include the confirmation and the internal processing step. Do not call the journey complete if the customer can tap Submit but staff cannot find the request or resolve a mistake.

Limit the first release deliberately

Separate essential functions from conveniences. Saved favourites might be valuable; a social feed probably does not help the reorder task. Prioritize features by how directly they support the core outcome and what evidence supports the need. A smaller scope should still include validation, accessibility and recovery from common errors.

Describe failure states

What should happen when a connection drops during submission? How does the user know whether an order was received? What if an item is discontinued? Write these behaviours into the brief. They are part of the product, not optional polish to add after the happy path is built.

Decide how to learn

Choose a few observations for the pilot: completed requests, abandoned steps and support questions. Interview users who stop midway. A release that reveals why people struggle can be more useful than a long feature list. Use those findings to decide whether the next investment should be another capability or a simpler existing flow.

Turn planning into action. Create an editable website brief or work through the launch checklist.
